newsitem.title: UK: Tanker rates from Mideast up on Iraqi crude sales.
newsitem.headline: Tanker rates from Mideast up on Iraqi crude sales.

text.p: Chartering rates were steady to firmer on Tuesday with enquiries to load Iraqi crude firming rates for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to the West, shipbrokers said.

Coastal was reported to have fixed the Stena Companion to load 350,000 tonne on August 15 at the Iraqi port of Mina al Bakr for voyage to the U.S. Gulf but no rate was reported and shipbrokers were unable to confirm the deal other than as subject to contract.
However, Similar tonnage was fixed from Ras Tanura to the U.S. Gulf by Chevron at a firm W60.
Brokers expected the return of Iraqi crude sales to also strengthen the market for million barrel vessels in the Mediterranean and West Africa early next week.
Several bookings for million barrel vessles were reported but as with the VLCCs no details could be confirmed.
"There is no doubt that shipowners will be looking to fix there million barrel vessels for the more profitable longer transatlantic voyages," a broker said.
Mediterranean activity was slow, but a flurry of business to the U.S. Gulf, U.S. East coast and UK/Cont/Med out of West Africa steadied West African rates around Mondays lower levels.
Recent focus of trade the Mideast to Singapore route was quieter but rates were assessed firmer at around W85.
Demand from U.S. oil refiners continued to support rates for shorter-haul crudes from Mexico and the Caribbean. Rates for 70,000 tonners from the to the U.S Gulf were steady around W145.
Inter UK-Cont routes for 80,000 tonners were slightly weaker at around W87.5 while a clutch of trips from the Baltic port of Ventspils were fixed at around W92.5-W95 for 80,000 tonners.
